concepts.learning_objective: Identify the characteristics that mark a society as a civilisation.
Place the beginnings of civilisation in Mesopotamia, Egypt and India in time.
Explain how fertile river plains led villages to grow into towns and cities around 2600 BCE.
Explain why the civilisation has several names and why its inhabitants are called Harappans.

topics.title: The Sarasvati River and Harappan Sites

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Sarasvati River, its present names and its mention in the Rig Veda.
Locate major Harappan cities and sites in their modern states or regions.
Describe the main features of Harappan town-planning, such as streets, fortifications and upper and lower towns.
Explain the structure of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro and the debate about its purpose.
Describe how Harappan houses, drains and wells reflect care for cleanliness and water.
Explain how the reservoirs of Dholavira harvested and stored water.
Identify the crops and farming tools of the Harappans and the link between villages and cities.
Explain how archaeological evidence reveals what the Harappans ate.
Identify Harappan exports, imports and trade routes, including the Lothal dockyard.
Describe Harappan seals and their likely link with trade.
Describe Harappan crafts such as carnelian beads, shell bangles and bronze.

topics.title: The Lives of the Ancients and the End of the Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Harappan objects of daily use and cultural or symbolic objects.
Explain the factors agreed upon for the decline of Harappan cities and what survived.
